claims.text: The as-fabricated HEA is a homogeneous single-phase solid solution.
The as-fabricated HEA has a homogeneous compositional distribution.
The as-fabricated HEA has an equiaxed grain structure.
Mechanical loading induces local compositional fluctuations in the HEA.
Mechanical loading induces strain localization in the HEA.
Loading-induced compositional fluctuations and strain localization trigger fine brittle precipitates along dislocation structures.
Loading-induced compositional fluctuations and strain localization trigger fine brittle precipitates at grain boundaries.
The brittle precipitates act as preferential crack-initiation sites.
Dislocation activity accelerates atomic diffusion in the HEA.
Accelerated atomic diffusion causes local concentration fluctuations.
Local concentration fluctuations nucleate secondary brittle phases or precipitates.
The secondary phases or precipitates weaken grain-boundary cohesion.
The secondary phases or precipitates accelerate crack propagation under continued loading.
Mechanically loaded samples will have lower fracture toughness than unloaded baseline samples.
Mechanically loaded samples will exhibit a higher incidence of brittle fracture than unloaded baseline samples.
Fine secondary phases or precipitates will be present in loaded samples and absent from the as-fabricated state.
The as-fabricated HEA has a ductile microstructure and high fracture toughness.
The proposed behavior manifests particularly at elevated temperature or under cyclic loading that promotes strain localization.
Under low-stress or low-temperature conditions, the HEA retains single-phase ductile performance.
The stress, temperature, and cycle-number thresholds for phase decomposition depend on alloy composition and processing history.
